chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Staying within the melody and improvisation
summary: She likes to stay close to melody; a good song needs no improvisation.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I like to stay within the melody with just maybe a little departure every once in awhile because I, so far as I'm concerned I feel that you can do too much of everything. From a singer's standpoint I like to, if there are one or two climax's in the rendition of a song, that's enough. Otherwise it gets too much. What do you do for an encore? That's just my approach. I think that I spend quite a bit of time deciding which numbers I like to do and how I'm going to do them. I like to think about the lyrics. I like to think about the progressions, you know, the changes and harmony. And I like the hear the good music in harmony, and sometimes singing a great melody on top of a beautiful harmony is a nice wedding, you know. I

also feel that when a good song is written it needs no improvisation. It's already a good song to begin with, so why play around with it. I guess that's one of the things that has never changed so far as I'm concerned, as so far as sticking to the melodies. I was complimented by Teddy Wilson once, you know, and Teddy is a very good musician, and he said, he remarked that I was one of the few singers that do the melodies of the song. But I like to learn the melody and then if I want to improvise I know where I'm going and how to get back. That may be a little inside talk, you know, as far as the musicians are concerned, but it is something to think about if I were - and I do have an opportunity to advise, work with some singers at different times. And one of the things I like to tell them is to learn the melody first, you know. They'll come in wanting to change it. So that's my approach. If it's a beautiful song I don't do anything but just sing it. And I think about how I'm going to quit.
